name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.not_singleton_amongNonUnital_of_infiniteDimensional
title: An infinite-dimensional unital algebra has no separable singleton model

content.display_title: An infinite-dimensional unital algebra has no separable singleton model
content.one_sentence_role: Uses the finite-dimensional algebra conclusion to contradict the proposed singleton condition.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be an infinite-dimensional nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital $*$-representation. Then $\pi$ cannot satisfy the singleton condition of R11.
content.assumptions: Infinite dimensionality is a hypothesis on $A$. The conclusion excludes the conjunction of nonzero irreducibility and unitary equivalence with every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation of $A$.
content.conclusion: The specified $\pi$ cannot represent a unique irreducible class. This does not rule out separable irreducible representations in general or construct a particular competing representation.
content.proof_summary: Assume the singleton condition and apply the preceding theorem for the dimension of the algebra.
proof_steps: If this $\pi$ satisfied the proposed condition, then [Finite dimension of the algebra from an unrestricted singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/OrdinarySingleton.lean#L96-L103) would apply: $A$ is nonzero and unital, $H$ is separable, and the assumed condition supplies its remaining input. It would give $\dim_{\mathbb C}A<\infty$, contrary to the stated infinite dimensionality. Therefore that condition cannot hold.
